amendments.rule: A one-token source unit takes that token as its source head. In a multi-source unit choose the lexical or syntactic head. **Where one morpheme in the unit carries content the others do not, that morpheme is the head, whatever its position.** A construct noun fused with its preposition heads the unit — `לִפְנֵי` → *before*, `בְּתוֹךְ` → *among* — exactly as rule 30 directs; a negation heads the unit it is fused into, as rule 35 heads a `וְ` + `לֹא` *Nor* on the negative and rule 48 heads `מֵאֵין` → *without* on the `אַיִן`; and a relative heads a resumptive fusion, as rule 22 heads `אֲשֶׁר בּוֹ` → *wherein* on the relative. **Where no morpheme carries content the others lack — a compound preposition written from two prepositions, or a pair of particles — the syntactic head decides, and that is the morpheme governing the rest, which in Hebrew is the one standing first**: `מֵאֵת` → *of*, `מֵעַל` → *from* or *against*, `כַּאֲשֶׁר` → *as* and `הַאִם` → *shall* each head on their opening morpheme. **The English word written is not what chooses a source head.** Rule 24's cross-language anchoring governs the target head alone, so do not move the source head onto the morpheme whose own sense the single English word happens to carry: one and the same `מֵעַל` rendered *from* in one verse and *against* in the next is one construction with one source head, and reading it off the translation would make the source analysis a function of the ASV's choice of preposition. Where two morphemes genuinely tie, choose and name the competing reading in the note under rule 8.
amendments.why: Rule 23 was a single sentence and said nothing about which morpheme heads a fusion when neither carries a lexeme, which is the gap NUM.17 fell into: the same מֵעַל headed on מִן in v5 and on עַל in v10, the second because against is עַל's sense — a target-side criterion rule 24 reserves for target heads. The amendment states the content test first, so rule 35's Nor on the negative, rule 48's מֵאֵין on the אַיִן, rule 22's wherein on the relative and rule 30's לִפְנֵי on the noun all keep the heads those rules already give them, and only the residue — two bare relational particles — falls to the governing morpheme. Evidence: five fused units in this chapter (מֵאֵת twice, מֵעַל twice, כַּאֲשֶׁר, הַאִם), which agree on the governing morpheme once v10 is corrected. The corpus tables report target heads only, so no corpus row bears on the question and none contradicts it.

conventions: Every compound preposition opening with מִן that the ASV renders by one English word is fused under rule 30 rather than split with one member unrepresented — מֵאֵת → of twice in v2, מֵעַל → from in v5, מֵעַל → against in v10 — and every one heads on the מִן, whichever preposition the ASV happened to write. v10 originally headed on עַל and was corrected in reconciliation. Where the ASV writes a second English word the fusion does not apply and the parts are split, as מִלִּפְנֵי → from before is in v9.

The chapter's distributive doublings are rendered once, and the count is read off what the Hebrew writes. מַטֶּה מַטֶּה in v2 has no אֶחָד beside it, so its two tokens carry rods and one; the fully repeated מַטֶּה לְנָשִׂיא אֶחָד of v6 leaves its second occurrence's four tokens unrepresented under rule 22. The supplied distributive each or every is placed on the noun it stands before under rule 15 — אָב in v2, נָשִׂיא in v6, אִישׁ in vv2 and 9 — and is never read as the rendering of the doubled מַטֶּה.

report: One real cross-verse split. The chapter fuses four compound prepositions opening with מִן — מֵאֵת → of (v2, twice), מֵעַל → from (v5), מֵעַל → against (v10) — and heads three of them on the מִן but v10 on the עַל. v5 and v10 are the same compound with the same 1cs suffix, so nothing in the source licenses the difference; v10's note chose a source head off the English word, which is rule 24's target-side criterion. Patched v10 to head that unit on s025 (מִן).
The mechanical table could not see this: it grouped מִן עַל as two treatments only because from and against differ, which is ASV-licensed. Reading the dump end to end is what shows it.

Corroborating chapter pattern: the chapter's other fused function-word pairs head on the governing morpheme (כַּאֲשֶׁר → as on כְּ in v11; הַאִם → shall on הֲ in v13), while pairs containing a lexical noun head on the noun (לִפְנֵי in vv4, 7, 9, 10; בְּתוֹךְ in v6). v10 was the only deviation.

Checked and found source-licensed rather than split: the הָיָה frames (v5 keeps that because no apodosis waw is written, v8 gives it to the waw that is — rule 45); the distributive doublings (v2 has no אֶחָד, so its second מַטֶּה takes one, while v6's fully repeated מַטֶּה לְנָשִׂיא אֶחָד leaves its second occurrence's four tokens unrepresented under rule 22); מִלִּפְנֵי split in v9 beside מֵאֵת and מֵעַל fused, since rule 30's one-rendering condition is met in one case and not the other; the added even in v6, which rule 16 requires because no marker stands on twelve rods; כָּתַב as write thou and thou shalt write; לְ as for, according to and there shall be for; the object marker unrepresented in all seven occurrences.

Examined and deliberately left: NUM.17.12 gives the subject pronoun we of the third clause to the suffix of כֻּלָּנוּ, while the two identical אָבַדְנוּ clauses beside it keep their own pronouns under rule 17. The suffix's presence is a real source difference, so this is not a split and I did not disturb an accepted edge; but the competing reading — the verb takes we are undone and the suffix is unrepresented under rule 22, as rule 43 disposes of two morphemes pointing at one referent — is defensible and is recorded here for whoever revisits the verse.
BSB: no comparable source occurrences for this chapter, so the comparison is unavailable rather than clean. There is no BSB disagreement to adjudicate and none was used to move an edge.
Ledger after the patch is unchanged in shape: 251 units, all 265 source and 327 target ids partitioned once; the patch changes one unit's source head only.
